The control fails only if real human writing scores significantly BELOW a model on grammar or consistency, which would mean the instrument is not measuring writing quality.

### Pairwise protocol: 299 usable comparisons, 1 unparseable

**Position-bias check.** Across all 298 decisive comparisons the judge chose the FIRST slot 124 times: 0.416 [0.362, 0.473]. Side assignment was randomised per comparison by a seeded RNG, so under no position bias this is 0.5. It is not, so the judge has a real slot preference; the per-comparison breakdown below shows whether that preference differs between the comparison types, which is what would actually distort the result.

| comparison type | decisive n | first-slot pick rate [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|
| main | 178 | 0.427 [0.357, 0.500] |
| null | 60 | 0.433 [0.316, 0.559] |
| ceiling | 60 | 0.367 [0.256, 0.493] |

A slot preference of the same size in every comparison type -- including the null, where the two arms are draws from the same distribution -- is an additive offset of the instrument. Because sides were randomised, such an offset cannot manufacture a win-rate difference between arms; it would have to differ between comparison types to do that.

**Tie-rate caveat.** The judge answered TIE on 0.3% of all comparisons, including when shown two DENSE seeds -- draws from the same distribution, where 'indistinguishable' is the truthful answer. So this judge will not use the tie option, and a low tie rate in the main test is not evidence of a real difference. The null control is the reference for what indistinguishable looks like on this instrument.

| comparison | n | wins left | wins right | ties | left win rate among decisive [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main: `dense_s0` vs `codes=512_s0` | 59 | 50 | 9 | 0 | 0.847 [0.735, 0.918] |
| main: `dense_s1` vs `codes=512_s1` | 60 | 49 | 10 | 1 | 0.831 [0.715, 0.905] |
| main: `dense_s2` vs `codes=512_s2` | 60 | 53 | 7 | 0 | 0.883 [0.778, 0.942] |
| **main: pooled** | 179 | 152 | 26 | 1 | 0.854 [0.795, 0.898] |
| null: `dense_s0` vs `dense_s1` | 60 | 31 | 29 | 0 | 0.517 [0.393, 0.638] |
| ceiling: `human` vs `dense_s0` | 60 | 56 | 4 | 0 | 0.933 [0.841, 0.974] |

Over all 179 dense-vs-discrete comparisons, counting ties as neither: dense wins 152, discrete wins 26, tie 1 (0.6% of comparisons).
Dense win rate among decisive comparisons: 0.854 [0.795, 0.898]. The 50% null is OUTSIDE the interval, so the judge can tell them apart.
